stem: A client with rheumatoid arthritis is starting oral methotrexate once weekly. Which additional teaching is most appropriate?

options.A: During a painful flare, take the prescribed weekly methotrexate dose on consecutive days until symptoms improve, then return to the usual weekly schedule.
options.B: Wait to begin folic or folinic acid until methotrexate adverse effects appear, because preventive supplementation can interfere with assessment of the starting dose.
options.C: Keep methotrexate on the weekly schedule but skip folic or folinic acid during the first treatment month so early therapeutic response can be evaluated without supplementation.
options.D: Keep methotrexate on the prescribed weekly schedule and take folic or folinic acid as directed to reduce the risk of selected methotrexate adverse reactions.

rationale: Current DailyMed methotrexate labeling for rheumatoid arthritis recommends a starting oral dosage of 7.5 mg once weekly with adjustment to achieve optimal response and specifically directs administration of folic acid or folinic acid to reduce the risk of methotrexate adverse reactions. The same labeling warns that medication errors involving incorrect methotrexate dosing have led to deaths, reinforcing the importance of maintaining the prescribed schedule rather than converting weekly therapy to daily dosing. Therefore D is correct. A introduces repeated daily dosing during a flare, which conflicts with the labeled weekly rheumatoid-arthritis regimen and creates a serious medication-error risk. B and C delay folate supplementation despite the current label's instruction to administer folic or folinic acid for adverse-reaction risk reduction; the label does not require waiting for toxicity or withholding supplementation during the first month.
educational_objective: Teach clients using low-dose methotrexate for rheumatoid arthritis to maintain the prescribed once-weekly schedule and take folic or folinic acid as directed to reduce selected adverse reactions.
source_organization: U.S. National Library of Medicine — DailyMed
source_version_date: SPL content dated July 24, 2026; current DailyMed labeling accessed 2026-08-25
source_locator: Dosage and Administration §2.1 Important Dosage and Safety Information: instruct patients and caregivers to take the recommended dosage as directed because medication errors have led to deaths. §2.3 Recommended Dosage for Rheumatoid Arthritis: recommended starting dosage is 7.5 mg orally once weekly with escalation to optimal response; administer folic acid or folinic acid to reduce the risk of methotrexate adverse reactions.
source_claim_supported: For rheumatoid arthritis, oral methotrexate is dosed once weekly and folic or folinic acid should be administered to reduce methotrexate adverse reactions; incorrect dosing can cause fatal medication errors.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)

correction_summary: Rebuilt all four teaching statements to remove the distractor-only absolute wording and make the alternatives realistic medication-safety errors. The final item is restricted to two directly labeled claims: once-weekly rheumatoid-arthritis dosing and folic/folinic-acid supplementation to reduce adverse reactions.

audit_findings.clinical_category: Rheumatoid arthritis pharmacotherapy — low-dose methotrexate schedule and folate supplementation
audit_findings.stem: PASS — specifies rheumatoid arthritis and an already prescribed once-weekly oral methotrexate regimen, focusing the item on additional safe-use teaching.
audit_findings.option_A: PASS as distractor — flare-driven dose adjustment may sound intuitive, but converting weekly methotrexate into consecutive daily dosing conflicts with the labeled regimen and creates a known fatal medication-error risk.
audit_findings.option_B: PASS as distractor — monitoring for adverse effects is important, but the label directs folic or folinic acid administration for risk reduction rather than waiting for toxicity to appear.
audit_findings.option_C: PASS as distractor — preserving weekly dosing is correct, but withholding folate for the first month is unsupported by the labeling and contradicts the supplementation instruction.
audit_findings.option_D: PASS — directly combines the labeled weekly schedule with labeled folic/folinic-acid supplementation; uniquely best.
audit_findings.ambiguity: PASS — D is the only response that preserves the prescribed schedule and implements supplementation without adding an unsupported delay or dose manipulation.
audit_findings.second_answer: EXCLUDED — A introduces unsafe daily dosing; B and C delay label-directed supplementation.
audit_findings.cueing: PASS — alternatives are comparable in length and clinical specificity and no distractor-only absolute term remains.
audit_findings.blueprint: PASS — NCSBN Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies directly includes safe medication administration, medication education, and adverse-effect prevention/recognition.
audit_findings.independent_adversarial_second_pass: PASS — challenged whether folate could reasonably be delayed to assess methotrexate efficacy or used only after adverse effects occur. Current 2026 DailyMed labeling directly instructs administration of folic acid or folinic acid to reduce adverse-reaction risk and separately specifies once-weekly rheumatoid-arthritis dosing, leaving D uniquely supported without adding a source-unsupported timing relationship between methotrexate and folate doses.
